analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (the changed range is head lines 3541-3575, a new section 'Cluster service listeners follow the cable and the pairing') and docs/developer/test.md (head lines 2465-2485, a test description). The head_text units for inference.md (lines 4919-5330+) are surrounding unchanged context, and I examined them without finding a changed security behavior. No executable source is in this batch, so no code-level regression can be shown from the evidence.

The documented behavior is a cluster-service listener lifecycle. Listeners restart or stop when the pairing store shows a new pairing, with a 5-second check interval. A listener on an earlier pairing refuses handshakes from a later pairing (handshakeRejected). A removed pairing stops both listeners. An unreadable pairing store changes nothing, which is fail-static (a running listener is kept). Pairing identity compares pins, label, link epoch and edge, never the edge secret. The old control node is dropped when the pairing changes. This reads as a hardening and availability fix: stale listeners are not left keyed to superseded pairings. One note: an unreadable store keeping the old listener running means a revoked or removed pairing might stay accepted while the store is unreadable. That is a design trade-off in code that is not supplied here. The control lease's listener restarts and stops without a log line, a minor auditability gap.

None of this touches the provider/coordinator WebSocket boundary (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041) or the add-on hold socket (TB-012). The cluster pairing and listener code (ClusterService.swift, ClusterSetupLinkExchange) was not supplied, so the actual implementation behavior (the stale-pairing window, port binding, the unreadable-store case) remains unverified. The next review pass should check that code if it appears in other batches, specifically the handshake key binding and how a removed pairing is handled when the store is unreadable. No findings.
